subject: MCPRouter.Shell - the Windows client, driven through the automation plane

controls.detail: all 7 declared section(s) publish an addressable container: settings.section.router, settings.section.harnesses, settings.section.sessionanalyst, settings.section.updates, settings.section.security, settings.section.ambientsurface, settings.section.advanced
named 'Launch router daemon at sign-in', toggle state readable as 'Off'
named 'Confirm before removing a server', toggle state readable as 'On'
named 'Show status in notification area', toggle state readable as 'On'

toggling 'Launch router daemon at sign-in' through the plane moved the board's state readout from 'LaunchAtLogin=off · RequireConfirmationOnDestructive=on · ShowAmbientIcon=on' to 'LaunchAtLogin=on · RequireConfirmationOnDestructive=on · ShowAmbientIcon=on' - an effect outside the control that was actuated.
Get-ScheduledTask reports no task at '\MCPRouter\WIN-SHELL Settings Witness (transient)' before the switch is driven, so the arms below measure THIS run's registration.
controls.recorder: Get-ScheduledTask (ScheduledTasks module over the Task Scheduler WMI provider)

controls.detail: driving the switch to On through the automation plane registered '\MCPRouter\WIN-SHELL Settings Witness (transient)' in the Windows task scheduler: state=Ready, logon trigger present, RunLevel=Limited (the recorder's word for the XML's LeastPrivilege), Execute=C:\Dev\mcp-router\app\windows\MCPRouter.Shell\win-shell-witness-daemon.exe. Read by an API that did not write it.
controls.recorder: Get-ScheduledTask (ScheduledTasks module over the Task Scheduler WMI provider)

controls.detail: C:\Dev\mcp-router\planning\evidence\WIN-SHELL\run\shell-state\shell-settings.json holds LaunchAtLogin=true, read off the disk by this script. The file is the recorder; the shell is not asked what it saved.
controls.recorder: a read of the settings file by this script

controls.detail: the shell was terminated and launched again as a new process, and the switch reads On in the new one. Closing the shell no longer forgets the setting.
controls.recorder: a second MCPRouter.Shell process, launched after the first was terminated

controls.detail: the clipboard held this lane's sentinel before the button was invoked and holds 'http://127.0.0.1:8879' after, read out of a separate PowerShell process. It matches the endpoint the board displays at settings.state.endpoint.
controls.recorder: Get-Clipboard in a separate PowerShell process

controls.detail: driving the switch back to Off removed '\MCPRouter\WIN-SHELL Settings Witness (transient)': Get-ScheduledTask reports absence again, so its yes above was a reading rather than an echo.
controls.recorder: Get-ScheduledTask (ScheduledTasks module over the Task Scheduler WMI provider)

controls.detail: with the switch driven Off, a separate process asks the shell for the icon at {0F5B6D3A-8C41-4E2B-9D77-2A6E5C1B4A90} and is told there is none (HRESULT 0x80004005). The recorder is capable of saying no, and any yes below is this run's.
controls.recorder: Shell_NotifyIconGetRect in a separate powershell.exe process

controls.detail: driving the switch to On through the automation plane put an icon in the Windows notification area at {0F5B6D3A-8C41-4E2B-9D77-2A6E5C1B4A90}: a separate process asked the shell for its rectangle and got 2076,1528 to 2124,1600 (HRESULT 0x00000000). Read by an API this application never called.
controls.recorder: Shell_NotifyIconGetRect in a separate powershell.exe process

controls.detail: driving the switch back to Off took the icon out of the notification area: the same reader that found it a moment ago now answers HRESULT 0x80004005. Its yes above was a reading rather than an echo, and turning the setting off tells the user something true.
controls.recorder: Shell_NotifyIconGetRect in a separate powershell.exe process

controls.detail: the router lists both servers this lane declared - lane-cleanup-delta, lane-witness-beta, lane-cleanup-gamma, lane-witness-alpha - before any removal is attempted, so the arms below measure removals rather than absences that were already there.
controls.recorder: the router's own /servers listing, read over the control API by this script

controls.detail: with the setting On, Remove raised a confirmation, this lane pressed 'Keep it', and the router still lists lane-witness-alpha (now: lane-cleanup-delta, lane-witness-beta, lane-cleanup-gamma, lane-witness-alpha). The refusal is read out of the router, not out of the dialog: the app's account of having asked is not evidence that it obeyed the answer.
controls.recorder: the router's own /servers listing, read over the control API by this script

controls.detail: pressing 'Remove permanently' removed lane-witness-alpha from the ROUTER - it now lists lane-cleanup-delta, lane-witness-beta, lane-cleanup-gamma. The gate opens as well as closes.
controls.recorder: the router's own /servers listing, read over the control API by this script

controls.detail: with the setting Off, Remove raised no confirmation at all and the router no longer lists lane-witness-beta (now: lane-cleanup-delta, lane-cleanup-gamma). The prompt above was the setting being obeyed rather than a dialog this board always shows.
controls.recorder: the router's own /servers listing, read over the control API by this script

controls.detail: the router lists both servers this lane declared for the Cleanup board - lane-cleanup-delta, lane-cleanup-gamma - before any removal is attempted from it, so the arms below measure removals rather than absences that were already there. Neither has ever been called, which is what puts them on this board at all: the rows come from the router's own usage figures now, not from sample data.
controls.recorder: the router's own /servers listing, read over the control API by this script

controls.detail: with the setting On, the Cleanup board's Remove selected raised a confirmation, this lane pressed 'Keep it', and the router still lists lane-cleanup-gamma (now: lane-cleanup-delta, lane-cleanup-gamma). The refusal is read out of the ROUTER, not out of the dialog: the app's account of having asked is not evidence that it obeyed the answer.
controls.recorder: the router's own /servers listing, read over the control API by this script

controls.detail: pressing 'Remove permanently' on the Cleanup board removed lane-cleanup-gamma from the ROUTER - it now lists lane-cleanup-delta. The board's button reaches the router at all, which is the half of DEF-302 no dialog check could establish.
controls.recorder: the router's own /servers listing, read over the control API by this script

controls.detail: with the setting Off, Remove selected raised no confirmation at all and the router no longer lists lane-cleanup-delta (now: nothing). The prompt above was THIS SETTING being obeyed by THIS board, rather than a dialog the Cleanup board always shows.
controls.recorder: the router's own /servers listing, read over the control API by this script

the router was stopped from outside the application - this script killed the process and then confirmed, over the loopback port, that nothing answers http://127.0.0.1:57690/status - and the shell's pane moved to 'Cannot reach router' / 'The router daemon is not responding on 127.0.0.1:57690.'. It does not say 'Router ready' over a router that is not running, which is DEF-301 exactly.
controls.recorder: UI Automation read of the shell pane, over a router state driven by starting and stopping processes outside the application

controls.detail: a process outside the application answered /status with three tool calls in flight across two upstreams, and the pane moved to 'Serving tool calls' / '3 active tool calls in flight.'. The count came from the answer, not from the app.
controls.recorder: UI Automation read of the shell pane, over a router state driven by starting and stopping processes outside the application

controls.detail: /status was answered with two upstreams in pendingAuth and the pane moved to 'Decisions waiting' / '2 servers are waiting for you to sign in.'.
controls.recorder: UI Automation read of the shell pane, over a router state driven by starting and stopping processes outside the application

controls.detail: the product's own router was started again outside the application and the pane moved to 'Router ready' / 'All systems quiet. No active calls or queued items.'. The surface reads the real router, not only the lane's stand-in.
controls.recorder: UI Automation read of the shell pane, over a router state driven by starting and stopping processes outside the application

controls.detail: taking the router away again put the pane back to 'Cannot reach router' / 'The router daemon is not responding on 127.0.0.1:57690.'. Its readings above were readings rather than a state it latched on to.
controls.recorder: UI Automation read of the shell pane, over a router state driven by starting and stopping processes outside the application

controls.detail: the router was stopped, replaced twice and started again underneath the running shell, and the shell was still on the automation plane at the end of it.
controls.recorder: UI Automation read of the shell pane, over a router state driven by starting and stopping processes outside the application

controls.detail: with no MCPRouter.Shell running at all, Explorer was restarted and a separate process asking the new notification area for {0F5B6D3A-8C41-4E2B-9D77-2A6E5C1B4A90} is told there is none (found=False, HRESULT 0x80004005). A fresh notification area does not invent this icon, so a yes below is about an icon that is in it.
controls.recorder: Shell_NotifyIconGetRect in a separate powershell.exe process, across an Explorer restart

controls.detail: the notification area held the icon at {0F5B6D3A-8C41-4E2B-9D77-2A6E5C1B4A90}, Explorer was killed and came back, and a separate powershell.exe asking the new shell for that GUID gets a rectangle again (2124,1528 to 2172,1600, HRESULT 0x00000000) - where the same reader, with nothing owning the icon, was told there was none. The icon comes back without the operator doing anything.
controls.recorder: Shell_NotifyIconGetRect in a separate powershell.exe process, across an Explorer restart
